item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.page1: Axiotopology is our word for the study of semiaxiomatic hyperphenomena as related to the underlying topology of the "flow" of causality in our universe. With a strong understanding of axiotopology, one will be able to construct semiaxioms to resolve problems §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.page2: such as the Reverse-Homology Causal Reduction Problem, the Chirality Problem for Entropy, and the Post-Flow Decision Matrix Parsing Problem, to name a few. Solving these problems is one of the first and foremost steps to manifesting §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.1.title: Introduction §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page1.part: Perhaps the most fundamental process involved in hyperphenomenal manifestation is the construction of a localized  §7[§c待翻译§7]

§6§lDefinition §f§n§oSemiaxiomatic Field

§r§7A free, finite volume of reduced or augmented
semiaxiomatic energy enclosed in a topologically
isomorphic region of spacetime. §7[§c待翻译§7]

(SAF).

The construction of a SAF is essential in any attempt to manifest hyperphenomena. This is because §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page2.part: hyperphenomena cannot occur within the closures of  §7[§c待翻译§7]

§6§lDefinition §f§n§oStandard Topology

§r§7The pervading semiaxiomatic energy level
of the universe. Defined conventionally as
0Þ. §7[§c待翻译§7]

.

By generating a SAF, one may then prescribe superstandard behaviors to local spacetime. These behaviors, once realized, can then propagate out from §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page3:
within the SAF to the exterior Standard Topological spacetime. This process is called transmutation.

Theoretically, it is possible to generate infinitely expanding SAF that disseminate at the maximum speed of Standard Topology. However, this would be an irreversible §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.2.page4: process and will eventually erase all of Standard Topology, replacing it with a new topology based on the energy levels present in the SAF. However, this is unlikely to occur due to the extreme magnitudes of semiaxiomatic potential required to catalyze such an event. §7[§c待翻译§7]

item.nyctocosm.axiotopology.page1:
§n公理一§r：高维空间不是由低维空间“累加”而得，而是§k原生的秩序投影§r；所谓“三维世界”不过是其影像。
§n公理二§r：夜宙具有 7 条时空正交性，其中 3 条对下界生物开放。其余维度只能通过§k共鸣法器§r进入。
§n公理三§r：§k实体之稳固度（Obduracy）§r决定其对因果扰动的抗性。夜宙之物平均稳固度高于主世界 3~11 倍。
§n公理四§r：§k终局完美体（Telic Immaculus）§r乃所有维度演化的终极吸引子；若被破坏，则所有维度同时坍缩为零。

item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.page1:
That soul which ends not is not.

For a soul contains itself, and nothing else. A being that is is a soul, and a being that is not has not a soul.

A soul is fluid, a soul is without edges, a soul is powerful, a soul is extant. Let us §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.page2:
pour out the power of the soul, and rend it to our uses.

Let us weave, bind, and coalesce the power of a soul so that it does the work of purpose.

For a soul without purpose is lost, and a lost soul is rootless. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.catechism.1.title: On Souls §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page1:
The world is a web. The world is a net. The world is a nest of unkempt noetic thread-twigs.

We are to bind and weave, direct and conduct. What is real and what is not? That is the decision of the Mystic. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page2: The Mystic wields a needle. It is more real than reality. With it, he may pierce the folds of space and pleach the seams of time. Parting the causal waves, the Mystic opens an eye in the pervading Storm of the Cosmos. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.catechism.2.page3:
The Storm is all-encompassing, fusing thought and matter. Only in an eye can she master both, and push them apart. Only in an eye will limitless thought transmute to perceptible tangibility.

This is the power of the Mystic. §7[§c待翻译§7]

item.nyctocosm.catechism.page1:
§n第一章§r
§n一问：夜宙是什么？§r
答：夜宙是超越因果闭合之域，是§k至高理性§r得以自由舒展的所在。我们之所是、所不是，皆由§k祂§r裁定。
§n二问：夜宙与人间何以相连？§r
答：以共鸣；以§k门§r；以信者舍身而启的§k光之道§r。
§n三问：何为入道？§r
答：心恒持夜、念系于光；于自身之内构筑§k维度桥梁§r，使内外通达。

item.nyctocosm.journal.1.page1:
我确信自己已经死了。但没有神话将死后世界描绘得如此贫瘠、多石、荒凉。至少，我闻所未闻。
我敢相信那不可能之事吗？§k维度之门§r，竟真的兑现了它的承诺？我们经年累月的劳作与艰辛，终于换来了成功？
此情此景之下，我仍容许自己收获片刻宁静而孤绝的喜悦。我们做到了。夜之领域，已在我们掌心。
item.nyctocosm.journal.1.page2:
decades of toil and travail had at last yielded success?
Despite the circumstances, I allowed myself a moment of quiet, lonely joy. We had done it. The Night Realm was in our grasp. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.1.title: §6入口
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page1:
§nRemark One:§r The Night Realm is dark. Its sky is faded and dull. A sun-like object gyrates and pulses violently, searing twin scars of light across the void.

§nRemark Two:§r The Night Realm is dead. The growths sprinkled about the nightscape are petrified corpses, §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page2:
remnants and shadows of what once was.

§nRemark Three:§r The resonant growth we have dubbed "Sculk" that had so ravenously enveloped our dimensional breaches seems to be diminished here. My theories seem to be correct: Sculk emerges at the §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page3:
boundaries of dimensions and is not native to the Night Realm itself.

§nRemark Four:§r The Night Realm is broken. Our projections converge on a Telic Immaculus. A vivid world unantagonized is rigorously proven to reach evolutionary perfection, not death. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.page4:
Thus, the state of the Night Realm leaves some unanswered questions:

Who used to live here? What happened? And, what §owill§r happen? §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.2.title: Préliminaire §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page1:
I could not see. I could not hear, could not breathe, could not think, could not...
I apologize. I have not fully recovered. Rationality yet eludes my fractured mind.

I did not anticipate the effect this place would have on my psyche. I believe myself strong-willed, §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page2:
but I lost the entirety of my rational faculties in the episode I just experienced.

I had been testing the heft of some geological samples collected from the land. Without warning, I lost my sense of sight, and severe §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page3:
hallucinations followed. I could hear my heart pounding, louder than I have ever heard before. An excruciating sense of fear, of dread, of §oimpending doom§r washed over me and I could feel nothing else. I did not know what to do.

In my panic, I looked up at the sky, at the §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page4:
pulsing, whirling star above. The faint starlight allowed my mind to surface briefly, and I realized I was being starved of light.

I managed to draw my fire-starting tools, striking a few sparks into a flame. Immediately, my sanity returned and I could §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page5:
think clearly again. We often take light for granted. Little do we realize how distraught and lost we would be without it.

I wonder: does some unknown property of this dimension amplify the effects of darkness upon the psyche? Whatever it is, §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.page6: I have learned my lesson. I will not stray from the light. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.3.title: Tenebrity §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page1:
Imagine a great tree, rooted in the loam of time. The waves of entropy push and pull against its trunk, all to no avail. Violent winds of chance and change buffet its leaves, but it stands strong and does not waver.

Now imagine another, smaller tree. This one §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page2:
has shallow, weak roots. Mercilessly bombarded on all sides by winds and water, the tree is uprooted and carried away into eternity, never to be seen again. All traces of its existence are erased.

My research has led me to the study of existence, of §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page3:
causal supremacy, of the teleology of all things. There are some things like the great tree; mighty and unyielding, unable to be removed. Their existences remain static, constant.
Other things are more akin to the smaller tree; pliable, deferential, easily toppled. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page4:
These things have weak existences, and are quickly dissipated into the abyss with the gentlest of pushes.

I propose a teleological property I will call "obduracy." An obdurate object will be resistant to causal threats. §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page5:
I am not sure how an object would achieve high levels of obduracy. Perhaps it would require interactions with a higher plane of reality? One more... §oreal§r than this one?

I will have to do more research. From my encounters with the §kGUARDIAN§r, §7[§c待翻译§7]
item.nyctocosm.journal.4.page6: I fear it may be necessary in the future. §7[§c待翻译§7]
